docs.title: Cobalt Fintech - 2026 Platform Renewal Proposal
content: Cobalt Fintech - 2026 Platform Renewal Proposal
Prepared for: Maya Chen, Chief Executive Officer. Copy: Victor Hale, Chief Financial Officer.
Date sent: 11/14/2026. Target close: 12/11/2026.
1. Summary
Renewal of the Cobalt Fintech platform subscription for 2026 at $320,000 per year (a 7% uplift on the current term).
2. Options
- Option A, one year: $320,000.
- Option B, three years: $304,000 per year (5% off the one-year price), with pricing locked for the full term.
3. Value delivered this term
- Adoption up 12% since the October QBR.
- API usage by Priya Nair's engineering team up quarter over quarter.
- Two open support escalations, each with a named owner and a fix date.
4. Open items
- Victor Hale asked for a two-year price lock as an alternative to the 7% uplift.
- Sara Kim (Procurement) reports a competitor quote 15% lower for the same seats.
- Tom Ruiz (General Counsel) flagged the uncapped data-breach liability clause; legal review in progress.
5. Next steps
- Renewal working session 11/19, renewal call 11/20.
- Redlined MSA to Tom Ruiz by 11/21.

docs.title: Cobalt Fintech - Master Subscription Agreement (Cobalt legal markup)
content: Master Subscription Agreement - Cobalt Fintech (renewal draft with Cobalt legal markup, 11/18/2026)
Section 4. Term and renewal. Initial term of one year from 1/1/2026; Cobalt proposes a three-year term at a fixed annual fee.
Section 5. Fees. Annual fee $320,000. Cobalt markup: price increases capped at 0% for years 2 and 3 (price lock).
Section 7. Payment. Net 30. Cobalt markup: Net 60.
Section 9. Limitation of liability.
9.1 (our draft) Each party's total liability is capped at the fees paid in the 12 months before the claim.
9.2 (Cobalt markup) Liability for data-breach claims is UNCAPPED and excluded from 9.1.
9.3 (Cobalt markup) Supplier indemnifies Cobalt for regulatory fines arising from any security incident.
Section 11. Termination for convenience. Cobalt markup: Cobalt may terminate on 90 days' notice after year one.
Section 14. Governing law: California.
Cobalt comment (Tom Ruiz): Sections 9.2 and 9.3 are required for our board. Please return your redline by 11/21.

docs.title: Legal playbook - customer contracts (2026)
content: Legal playbook - customer contracts (2026). Owner: Hannah Ortiz, General Counsel.
Limitation of liability
- Standard: each party's liability capped at fees paid in the prior 12 months.
- Fallback 1: data-breach claims capped at 2x annual fees (super-cap). AE may offer with Legal review.
- Fallback 2: data-breach super-cap up to 3x annual fees. Needs General Counsel approval.
- Uncapped liability: not standard. Needs General Counsel AND CFO approval, and is limited to gross negligence.
Indemnities
- We indemnify for third-party IP claims. We do not indemnify customers for regulatory fines.
Payment terms
- Standard Net 30. Net 45 with Deal Desk approval. Net 60 needs CFO approval.
Price protection
- Renewal uplift caps of up to 5% may be offered by the AE. Price locks of two years or more need Deal Desk approval.
Termination
- No termination for convenience in the first term. Any exception needs General Counsel approval.

docs.title: Discount policy - multi-year deals (FY27)
content: Discount policy - multi-year deals (FY27). Owner: Deal Desk.
Approval levels (discount off list, total contract value)
- Up to 10%: Account Executive.
- Over 10% up to 20%: Sales Manager.
- Over 20%: VP Sales (Pat Rivera) AND Deal Desk.
- Over 30%: also needs CFO (Marcus Webb).
Multi-year guidance
- Two-year term: up to 8% off the one-year price.
- Three-year term: up to 15% off the one-year price.
- Price locks of two years or more need Deal Desk sign-off regardless of discount.
